newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Thousands demand Islamic state in S. Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Thousands demand Islamic state in S. Philippines.

text.p: Tens of thousands of Filipino Moslems on Wednesday demanded a separate state in one of the biggest Islamic rallies in the southern Philippines.

Many in the crowd, estimated by the military at 50,000 and by reporters at 200,000, chanted "Allaho Akbar" (God is Great) when a speaker read a paper calling for an independent Islamic state for the mainly Roman Catholic country's five million Moslem minority.
Another group called for self-determination for Moslems.
The rally in Sultan Kudarat town, Maguindanao province, capped a two-day assembly organised by private Moslem groups, including local religious leaders and professionals.
Crowds stretched for about a kilometre (0.6 mile) with many gathering in groups on both sides of a highway near the rally site, according to witnesses.
Organisers said one million people registered for the two-day gathering, including tens of thousands from other provinces in the Mindanao region, 800 km (500 miles) south of Manila.
Dozens in the crowd carried signs reading "In an Islamic state, everybody is equal" and "Koran is our constitution."
Rally leader Abousayed Mansur Lingga dismissed suggestions the rally was organised by the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), an insurgent group fighting for an Islamic state in Mindanao.

The rally occurred two months after President Fidel Ramos's government signed a peace deal with the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) ending a 24-year, MNLF-led revolt for Moslem autonomy in the southern islands.

As part of the deal, MNLF chairman Nur Misuari was elected governor of a semi-autonomous region comprising four Moslem provinces. Ramos has also installed him as head of a council supervising development projects in the southern region.
The MILF, a breakaway MNLF faction and considered by the military to be a hard-line group, is not part of the accord. Some of its leaders have accused Misuari of selling out to Manila.
The government has started exploratory talks with the MILF to try to negotiate a separate deal with them.
"This is a forum to ventilate new ideas and ... recommend a just, viable and lasting solution to the problems of Mindanao," Lingga told reporters.
Filipino Moslems regard Mindanao as their ancestral homeland although they are outnumbered 3-1 by Christians who have migrated to the region over several decades.
The Moslems have accused Christians of grabbing their lands and Manila of giving more attention to Christian-ruled provinces and neglecting Moslem areas.
The day-long rally, watched by about two dozen policemen, was peaceful.
